findings.title: New regression test is flaky (~8% failure rate)
findings.claim: The server fiber does sink.close() then drains source(), and the test does a bare server_done.get(); when stream_close() causes the reader to hit EOF, _stream_queue.abort() discards the queued eof marker and source() throws rpc::stream_closed, which escapes the test body uncaught (existing tests wrap this in check_exception). Measured 7/60 standalone failures and 2/12 whole-suite failures at --mode=dev -c2.

findings.title: test_data_sink_impl override breaks build at SEASTAR_API_LEVEL < 9
findings.claim: test_data_sink_impl unconditionally overrides put(std::span<temporary_buffer<char>>), but below API level 9 the pure virtual is put(net::packet), so compiling with --api-level 8 fails with 'marked override, but does not override'; loopback_socket.hh already guards the equivalent method with #if SEASTAR_API_LEVEL >= 9.

findings.title: Queue-drain half of the fix has no dedicated test coverage
findings.claim: The new test only exercises the case where close() is parked with an empty queue, so the drain logic is a no-op in that test; reverting just the drain leaves the whole suite green even though the stress case then segfaults 3/5, meaning a deterministic test with a parked data_sink and queued bytes blocking write() on _in_batch is still needed.

findings.title: hook_capturing_compressor_factory mutates a shared vector from two shards
findings.claim: The factory is shared across shards, and negotiate() const_casts and push_backs into it from both shard 0 (parent connection) and shard 1 (stream connection); no failure is observable today because server hooks are unused and negotiations are ordered by the smp::submit_to chain.

findings.title: _stream_queue.abort() discards the received eof marker on clean stream close
findings.claim: A cleanly closed stream can surface as rpc::stream_closed rather than an unengaged optional; this pre-dates the PR and is already worked around in apps/rpc_tester/rpc_tester.cc, but it is the root cause of the flaky test finding.

findings.title: Docs don't mention that a clean stream close can surface as a throw
findings.claim: The new 'Closing a stream' section tells callers to read until eof 'or throws' but never states that a clean close can itself be the thing that throws; a sentence should be added there and on rpc::source since this is now the normal case.

findings.title: Suspected stream_close() deadlock via _outgoing_queue_ready when _negotiated is unresolved
findings.claim: The reviewer suspected a deadlock but rejected it after investigation: every path reaching stream_close() implies negotiation completed, and stop_send_loop() still serializes via _sink_closed_future.

findings.title: Doxygen block placement questioned
findings.claim: The reviewer flagged the doxygen block placement in rpc_types.hh but rejected it as a non-issue after investigation.

findings.title: Unguarded _connected deref in abort()
findings.claim: The reviewer considered an unguarded _connected dereference in abort() but rejected it as pre-existing and an unreachable path.

findings.title: PR description contains a Claude Code attribution line
findings.claim: The PR description carries a '🤖 Generated with Claude Code' line, which the user's own global instructions say should never be added.
